title: Export-market mix
description:
## Background
NSW Coal Atlas is a static Three.js application. The current commercial dataset in dist/data/industry.json contains 35 registry mine records (snapshot 2026-09-11), three reported production complexes, five destinations and twelve schematic source-linked relationships. It has operators for 33 records. Existing geology, borehole exploration and the corrected terrain must remain available. The user explicitly chose commercial insight over further scientific-rigour work on 12 September 2026.

## Goal and rationale
Show aggregate destination-country exposure for NSW coal trade. Adds the demand-side geography absent from the mine inventory. Product-confidence judgment: 83%, not a statistical estimate. Priority rank 13 of 15 retained commercial ideas.

## Design and delivery
Find an official coal-only NSW or port trade series with country, period, mass/value basis and licence. Build ranked bars and period comparison, clearly separated from mine-level relationships. Keep country attribution at the exact source scope.

## Boundaries and risks
Port, state and customs datasets have different boundaries. Country totals do not reveal individual mine customers.

## Existing implementation to extend
Extend the static industry inventory and commercial modules; use explicit source-linked data structures rather than a new service until a live feed is justified.

## Acceptance
Deliver a working user flow with visible units, reporting periods, data scope and missing-data behavior. Preserve all existing geology controls, industry filters, source links and exports. Do not introduce geological validation work or fabricate missing commercial inputs.

## Verification
Use pure tests for data transformations and real-browser tests for interactions and exports. Log inputs, expected and actual results, dataset snapshot, console errors and failed assets. Keep curated screenshots for desktop and mobile; omit temporary downloads from Git.
